endorsements.quote: First, applications should be classified through risk stratification, distinguishing between educational, research, operational, and clinical use cases.
Third, privacy and cybersecurity assessment should evaluate data handling, authentication, and potential vulnerabilities introduced through automated code generation.
Finally, post-deployment monitoring, maintenance responsibility, and lifecycle management (including update and retirement planning) should be explicitly assigned.

unlisted_practices: Conduct code inspection and dependency analysis of AI-generated code before institutional deployment of end-user-developed applications.
Ensure infrastructure approval aligns end-user-developed applications with institutional hosting standards, identity management systems, and approved cloud environments.
Validate usability and workflow alignment of end-user-developed applications with intended end-user needs before deployment.
Require a human expert, office, or formal review process to take accountable responsibility for the decision to deploy AI-generated code, since responsibility cannot be outsourced to AI.
Distinguish what end users can do with AI assistance from what requires accountable institutional expertise, and do not block end-user development entirely.
Apply more stringent safeguards from the start to high-risk clinical systems integrated into EHRs, patient portals, diagnostic workflows, or treatment decisions.
